title: The Sleeper Below
subtitle: The first ritual — and the first word from the deep.

customObject.name: geomantic anchor
customObject.description: the first ritual anchor — a stone ring, three turning bands, and a crystal that answers the deep

script.note: MAP: a ritual chamber at the edge of the drowned city — reachable through the crypt. Black water beyond the stone ring. The anchor stands ready; the Weaver of Form burns gold in the dark.

script.text: Set your feet where the stone is oldest, Architect. What we do now has not been attempted in the memory of any living thing — we are going to renovate a nightmare.
The Ritual of Ethereal Light. One anchor, one beam, one room of his prison made gentle. Tell me again this won't wake him angry.
I will not tell you that. I will tell you what I told the builders of the first temples: nothing that lives is soothed by darkness forever, and nothing that suffers is worsened by one kind light.

script.note: OBJECTIVE — Begin the Ritual of Ethereal Light. The bands of the anchor start to turn; the crystal brightens; a slow column of light climbs into the black water.

script.text: Now. Breathe with the stone. Let the geometry remember what a sanctuary is.

script.note: The light touches the first street of R'lyeh. Far below, something enormous stops moving. The water goes utterly still.
The voice is not a roar. It is vast and slow and tired — the sound of something that has not been spoken to in a very long time.

script.text: Not a grave. Not any more, if we can help it. We're not here to wake you, and we're not here to slay you. We're here to fix the house.
Fix. The little word of little hands. My house is made of my own despair, small builder. Every angle of it hates me, because every angle of it is mine.
Then let other hands hold other angles, Old One. A prison that mirrors its prisoner can mirror his healing just as faithfully. That is all a sanctuary is.
I dreamed of drowning cities. Of small minds cracking like shells. They tell each other I chose those dreams. I do not remember choosing anything… except, once, very long ago, a place to rest.
And the resting place went wrong, and everything after it went wrong, and the whole world called the result a monster.
…You speak of me as if I were a house with bad foundations.
I'm a builder. It's the kindest thing I know how to say — nothing built wrong has to stay wrong.

script.note: The column of light steadies. Below, one impossible spire slowly rights itself — the first stone of R'lyeh to stand straight in an aeon.

script.text: …Light. I had a name for it once, before the deep ate all my names. It does not burn. Why does it not burn?
Because it was made for you, and not against you. That is the whole difference, Old One — in light, and in cities, and in every made thing that ever held a soul.
Then build, little hands. Build slowly. I have been a long time in the dark… and I would not like to be disappointed again.

script.note: RITUAL COMPLETE — one district of R'lyeh glows faint and calm beneath the water. The Sleeper's breathing — if it is breathing — has slowed. The anchor keeps turning.

script.text: One room done. A city to go. Let's not disappoint him.
